reports.title: Fine-tuning in 3D
reports.question: Does a 3D equivariant encoder pre-trained on 19 million conformers beat the best frozen encoder?
reports.takeaway: Against its own comparators the paper's claim holds, ahead of fine-tuned CheMeleon on 38 of 45 combinations. Against Monroe + TabPFN 3 the data sets disagree: it leads on ExpansionRx and trails on Biogen, and what it wins it wins through fine-tuning, not the frozen encoder.
reports.summary: Atom-JEPA pre-trains a 39M-parameter EquiformerV3 by latent prediction on 19M Uni-Mol conformers and fine-tunes it, multitask, on ten conformers per molecule. It is run here with the authors' own code and released weights, against the arm the paper did not run, Monroe + TabPFN 3, and a frozen Atom-JEPA arm read by the same TabPFN 3 call separates the representation from the fine-tuning.
reports.finding: Fine-tuned Atom-JEPA is ahead of fine-tuned CheMeleon on 38 of 45 combinations and of LightGBM on all 45. Against Monroe it is ahead on 6 of 9 ExpansionRx endpoints and behind on 4 of 6 Biogen ones, and training-set size does not explain the split (ρ = −0.04). Frozen, its embedding never beats Monroe's, a median −0.09 R²; fine-tuning never loses to freezing and adds +0.13 on ExpansionRx and +0.07 on Biogen.
